Definition: passed, i.e. kept over; used only of stored grain
BiblicalUsage: This word for stored grain — the old corn of the land — occurs only in Joshua 5:11-12. The day after the Passover, Israel eats 'of the old corn of the land... unleavened cakes, and parched corn in the selfsame day. And the manna ceased on the morrow after they had eaten of the old corn of the land.'
TheologicalSignificance: The manna stops the day Israel eats the old corn — forty years of daily bread ends, and the land feeds them instead — and I believe that is the moment the wilderness ends.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
